title: Spanish — Lección preliminar Quiz
subtitle: Parts 1 and 2 · greetings and introductions
notes: Lección preliminar, parts 1 and 2. Transcribed verbatim from the teacher's answer key. The key is the authority.
Trailing periods are inconsistent in the key — "Hasta luego" has none, "Adiós." does. Do not normalize them.
The English parentheticals are the only thing separating six otherwise identical items: familiar from formal, and "your name" from "his/her name". Removing them makes those questions unanswerable.
One correction to the guide: it prints "Encantado(a" with a truncated parenthesis.

confusables are shown after a second miss. These are the pairs where a wrong answer is usually a real confusion rather than a blank, so "wrong" is not useful on its own: the note names the distinction instead.
notes is documentation for whoever edits this file. The engine ignores it.

confusables.note: Bien. is "well." Muy bien adds muy, "very" — "very well."
Both are middling answers. On this quiz Regular. is "okay" and Más o menos. is "so-so."
¿Qué tal? asks how things are going. ¿Qué pasa? asks what is happening.
All four belong to an introduction. Mucho gusto is "nice to meet you," Igualmente. is "likewise," El gusto es mío. is "the pleasure is mine," and Encantado(a) is "delighted."
Both ask how someone is. ¿Cómo estás? is familiar — for a friend. ¿Cómo está usted? is formal, and usted is the giveaway.
Both mean "and you?" Tú is familiar; usted is formal.
Te asks the person in front of you: "what is your name?" Se asks about someone else: "what is his/her name?"
Me llamo is "my name is." Se llama... is "his/her name is." Me is about me, se is about someone else.
